trip.name: Manila — Winter 2026
trip.dateNote: Dates below are the CURRENT TARGET, not booked. Jordan is aiming at November; the exact window is his call. Everything downstream (watchers, Travel Brief, this hub) derives from this file — so changing the dates here changes the whole suite.
trip.vibe: Two halves by design — Manila for the city and the food, then Zambales for the coast. Subic Bay Freeport is the resort-convenient option (it is IN Zambales, ~2.5h from Manila); the open Zambales coast is the more rustic one. Same province, different trip.

legs.purpose: City week — food, history, Intramuros, and the base for the whole trip
Coast — Subic Bay Freeport for resort convenience, or the open Zambales coast for the quieter version

flights.notes: letsfg, verified 2026-09-30 for a real November window: $1,225 Frontier (51h42m — DISQUALIFIED), $1,265 Breeze ($30h59m), $1,314 United (21h07m). Under rule 12 the United option is the honest pick. Benchmark says $1,100–1,400 is 'Fair' — we are mid-range, not overpaying.
Book as part of the same round trip. Returns from Manila.

budget.note: Flight is the single biggest line (~$1,300). Philippines is cheap once you land — the daily cost is a fraction of US prices, so the airfare is the whole game.

foodToLookForwardTo.title: Filipino food worth the flight
foodToLookForwardTo.note: The dish list, plus one Zambales-specific reason to go south.

items.what: Whole roast pig, crisp skin — the celebration dish, and the national obsession.
Soy, vinegar, garlic, bay. The everyday national dish and the one to learn first.
Sour tamarind soup — the one you will want on a humid day.
Peanut oxtail stew with bagoong (fermented shrimp paste) on the side.
Sizzling chopped pork with calamansi and chili — a Pampanga export, everywhere in Manila.
Noodles — long life, and at every birthday table.
Spring rolls, fresh or fried. The party food.
Shaved ice, evaporated milk, ube, leche flan, jackfruit. The heat-beater.
Cured beef, garlic fried rice, egg. Breakfast, and a reason to get up.
The notorious one. Optional. Nobody is grading you.
Zambales grows the Dinamulag — widely called the sweetest mango in the Philippines. You are going to the right province for it.

costComparison.title: Cost of Living: Philippines vs Cincinnati
costComparison.note: How far your money goes once you land

summary.verdict: Budget-friendly — the airfare is the cost; everything after landing is cheap.

entryChecklist.title: Philippines Entry — Checklist
entryChecklist.note: US passport = 30 days visa-free under EO 408. No visa needed.

items.item: Proof of funds if asked (bank statement / card on phone)
Cash rule: up to US$10,000 (or PHP 50,000) without declaring

days.title: Fly out
activities: Connect via a major carrier — watch the layovers, not just the total
days.notes: Under rule 12 the target is a ~1–1.5h connection and a total under 30h. A 51-hour routing is the same trip with a day and a half taken out of it.

days.title: Land in Manila
days.notes: First full day is recovery, not sightseeing. Manila traffic is real — build the buffer in.

days.title: South to the coast
days.notes: Subic Bay Freeport is inside Zambales — the resort option. The open coast is the quieter one. Same province.

days.title: Departure
days.notes: Leave the buffer day — the drive back from Zambales is not the place to be tight.

mustTry.name: Jollibee
mustTry.vibe: Every Filipino's first stop. Order it once, understand the country.

mustTry.name: Aristocrat
mustTry.vibe: Manila institution since 1936 — the chicken barbecue is the reason.

mustTry.name: Max's Restaurant
mustTry.vibe: Famous for the fried chicken — 'the house that fried chicken built.'

mustTry.name: Halo-halo spot (Razon's style)
mustTry.vibe: The heat-beater. First time here, order it and stop asking questions.

mustTry.name: Local carinderia
mustTry.vibe: The cheapest real meal you'll eat — point at what looks good.
mustTry.order: Whatever is on the tray: adobo, sinigang, pancit

nearby: Lechon — ask locally where the good whole-roast spot is; it is a celebration dish
Sisig — sizzling plate, everywhere in Manila
Tapsilog — the breakfast that starts the day right
Zambales mangoes when you get south — Dinamulag, the sweetest in the country

parks.name: Rizal Park (Luneta)
parks.note: The historic heart of Manila — the national monument and the green lung of the city.

parks.name: Paco Park
parks.note: Old circular cemetery turned quiet garden. A calm hour inside a loud city.

parks.name: La Mesa Eco Park
parks.note: Forest and reservoir north of the city — the one place that feels like woods.

malls.name: SM Mall of Asia
malls.note: One of the largest malls in the world, on Manila Bay. Go for the sunset.

malls.name: Greenbelt (Makati)
malls.note: The upscale one — gardens, restaurants, the polished side of Metro Manila.

malls.name: Robinsons Place Manila
malls.note: Central and easy, close to the Ermita/museum district.

bgc.name: Bonifacio High Street
bgc.note: Pedestrian strip in BGC — walkable, safe, and where Manila looks most modern.

bgc.name: The Mind Museum
bgc.note: Science museum in BGC. Good rainy-afternoon plan.

bgc.name: Venice Grand Canal Mall
bgc.note: Italian-themed mall at McKinley Hill — a canal, gondolas, and a novelty worth an hour.

packing.item: Rain shell — November still sees rain
Comfortable walking shoes (Manila is a walking city)
Universal power adapter (PH is 220V, type A/B)
Card + enough cash for the first two days

tips: Manila traffic is real — give any airport run a generous buffer, especially the return.
Under-30-days visa-free with a US passport, but the onward ticket is checked: have it ready.
eTravel registration is free and mandatory — do it inside 72h of departure, not earlier.
Grab is the Uber equivalent and works everywhere; you rarely need a street taxi.
A local SIM (Globe or Smart) is a few dollars for 30 days of data — get one at the airport.
PHP is the currency everywhere; cards work in malls and hotels, cash for street food and markets.
Zambales is ~2.5 hours from Manila — Subic Bay Freeport is INSIDE Zambales, so 'Subic vs Zambales' is resort-convenient vs beach-rustic, not two different provinces.
Rule 12 for the flight: aim for a ~1-1.5h layover and a total under 30h — a 51-hour routing is the same trip with a day and a half removed.
Book direct with the airline, not an OTA. It matters the day something goes wrong.
Mangoes in Zambales are the point. Ask for Dinamulag.
